subject: Cross-zone deep dive — availability scrub & ops plan
messages:
From: Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com
Cc: Tom Becker <tom.becker@acme.com>
Date: 2027-04-05T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Cross-zone deep dive — availability scrub

Hi Chloe,

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Acme is ready to move to a POC kickoff focused on the hands-on deep dive: prompt review, routing behavior, and a short load rehearsal to validate latency under our mix. We have stakeholders across NA/EU/APAC and want to line up a rotating schedule so each region gets at least one live session during their work hours.

High-level asks from our side:
- 90m hands-on sessions (walkthrough + live prompt testing)
- 60m load rehearsal with synthetic traffic and cache warm-up
- A short routing + failover tabletop (15m) integrated into the runbook

People: Tom (engineering lead, PST), me (product owner, CST), and our infra lead in Dublin (will confirm).

Can you propose a 2-week window with rotating start times so we can accommodate EU/APAC? Also, do you have a suggested agenda and any pre-test checklist we should run ahead of the load rehearsal?

Thanks — Liz

--
Liz Harper
Senior Product Manager | Acme Corp
liz.harper@acme.com
From: chloe_martin@redwood.com
To: Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-05T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Cross-zone deep dive — availability scrub

Hi Liz — delighted to kick this off. Outlined a practical approach below and attached a draft agenda (redwood-poc-agenda.pdf).

Proposal:
- Two-week POC window starting Mon 2027-04-12.
- Three hands-on sessions per week: one early-PST (to cover NA), one midday-UTC (EU overlap), one late-UTC / morning APAC (rotating so APAC can join). Each session 90m + optional 30m office hours.
- Single 60m load rehearsal in week 2 after an agreed warm-up period (we recommend a 24–48h cache warm-up).
- 15m routing/failover tabletop immediately following one of the hands-on sessions (we can record).

Practical asks for your ops team:
- Provide a short list of 3 representative prompt sets and expected throughput targets for load tests.
- Confirm the Dublin infra lead name/email for invites (we'll add timezone-specific calendar blocks).

Internal notes: Kar may propose a compact load plan and Jordan will manage capacity & runbook. Naomi — please hold tentative slots on the calendar and I will send a Doodle if Acme prefers a poll.

Options (all times in UTC for clarity):
- Option A: 16:00 UTC (08:00 PDT / 17:00 CET) — NA/EU overlap
- Option B: 00:30 UTC (16:30 PDT previous day / 09:30 AEST) — APAC friendly
- Option C: 12:00 UTC (04:00 PDT / 13:00 CET) — mid-day EU

If any of those look off, tell us rough windows for each region and we will map to rotating concrete slots.

Attachments: redwood-poc-agenda.pdf (draft), includes session objectives, prep checklist, and suggested synthetic traffic profile.

Cheers,
Chloe

--
Chloe Martin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
chloe_martin@redwood.com
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-05T13:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Cross-zone deep dive — availability scrub

Hey all — quick operational confirmation from infra side.

We can support the 90m hands-on + 60m load rehearsal. A few notes:
- For realistic load runs we prefer two warm-up windows: a short 6-hour prefix run and a longer 24-hour pre-warm if your cache-sensitive workloads rely on prefix KV caching.
- Proposed load profile (attached): 70% typical prompt fanout, 30% high-concurrency bursts. See loadtest-plan.xlsx.
- Suggest splitting load rehearsal into two 30m blocks (steady then spike) to isolate latency vs tail behaviors.

Scheduling suggestion: instead of fixed daily times, we recommend a rotating matrix: Week A (NA morning / EU late afternoon / APAC night-friendly), Week B shift by +8 hours to make APAC morning friendly. This keeps the ops burden low and gives each region at least one live slot during business hours.

I can be on the hands-on sessions for routing tests — will prepare the runbook snippets for failover (routing policy, fallback model, fallthrough metrics).

Regards,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Platform Engineer, Inference Ops | Redwood Inference
From: Tom Becker <tom.becker@acme.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Liz Harper <liz.harper@acme.com>, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-06T15:03:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Cross-zone deep dive — availability scrub

Chloe / Karthik — thanks, this looks good. We reviewed the agenda and the load plan internally and prefer Option A for the majority of hands-on sessions (16:00 UTC). A few quick items before you lock calendar invites: 

1) Token / rate guardrails — can you confirm per-minute token limits during the rehearsal and whether Redwood can temporarily raise them for the spike window?
2) Can you run a quick warm-up run the day before the full rehearsal (30m steady traffic) so we can validate instrumentation and logs?
3) SSO / account access: we've attached acme-sso-questions.docx with a short checklist; can you confirm the SAML metadata endpoint and the expected onboarding lead?

We can commit to the two-week window starting 2027-04-12. Please send calendar invites and a short mutual action plan (dates, owners).

If it helps, here's a shared folder with our internal readiness docs: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-POC-resources

Tom

--
Tom Becker
Engineering Lead, ML Platform | Acme Corp
